ambiguities.aspect: Signed representation of operands and result (two's complement vs sign-magnitude)
readings: a and b are two's-complement values and c = a + b truncated to N bits; the 'MSB' is just the natural sign bit and the absolute-value add/subtract description is only an implementation hint

a and b are sign-magnitude values (MSB = sign, lower N-1 bits = magnitude, fractional bits = Q) and c is also sign-magnitude, so a negative result must be encoded as {1'b1, |a-b| magnitude}, giving entirely different output bits than two's-complement arithmetic

ambiguities.aspect: Overflow/carry behaviour when the sum exceeds N bits
readings: Result wraps/truncates to N bits (carry-out discarded, sign bit taken from bit N-1 of the N-bit result), per 'MSB of the result is set to match the MSBs of a and b'
Result saturates to the most positive (N-1'h7FFF... / sign-magnitude max) or most negative value when overflow is detected by comparing sign bits of inputs and sum
Result keeps full N+1 bits internally and is shifted right by Q / rescaled before truncation, changing the numeric value of c

ambiguities.aspect: Output latency of c relative to a/b (registered vs combinational) and reset value of res
readings: c is a purely combinational function of a and b; res is only a named wire/alias and there is no clock, so c changes in the same cycle as a/b
c is the registered output res, updated one clock edge after a/b, with res power-up/reset value unspecified (0 vs X) so c is undefined for the first cycle after reset

ambiguities.aspect: Sign of the result and basis of comparison in the mixed-sign (and equal-magnitude) case
readings: Compare absolute values: if |a| > |b| take a-b with MSB forced to 0; if |b| > |a| take b-a with MSB=1; if |a| == |b| output +0 (all zeros)

Compare the signed values directly (a > b, b > a): for a == -b the phrase 'MSB set according to whether the result is zero or negative' permits emitting negative zero (MSB=1, magnitude 0), and the tie case is not specified at all
